clues: This city sits on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea in the southeast of Spain. Hills rise on one side and a river bed lies on the other.
A small desert sits right next to this city, so its air stays very dry. For Europe, that dry air is rare and stands out.
Caliph Abd al-Rahman III founded this city in 955. It then grew rich and became known around the world.
Its busy port once traded silk, oil, and raisins with far off lands. That trade made the city rich and well known.
Its port now sends more and more ships with people to North Africa. Boats cross the sea to lands like Morocco and Algeria.
